Sweet Azuki Bean Soup (Zenzai)

Served at: Dondoyaki Bonfire

Serves 4-6Prep 8 hours (or overnight) for soaking, plus 15 min activeCook 1 hour 30 min

Zenzai, a comforting sweet red bean soup, is a beloved treat in Japan, especially during winter festivals like Dondoyaki. Served warm with toasted mochi, it offers a delightful contrast of textures and a sweet, earthy flavor, perfect for warming up while watching the bonfire and reflecting on good fortune for the new year.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (200g) dried azuki beans
  • 6-8 cups (1.5-2 liters) water, plus more for soaking
  • 1/2 to 3/4 cup (100-150g) granulated sugar, to taste
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.25g) salt
  • 4-6 pieces kirimochi (square mochi cakes) or fresh mochi

Method

  1. Rinse the azuki beans thoroughly under cold running water.
  2. Place the rinsed beans in a large bowl and cover with plenty of cold water (at least 3 times the volume of the beans). Soak for at least 8 hours or overnight. Alternatively, for a quick soak, bring beans and water to a boil, boil for 5 minutes, then turn off heat and let sit for 1 hour.
  3. Drain the soaking water from the beans and discard it.
  4. Transfer the drained beans to a large pot and add 6 cups (1.5 liters) of fresh cold water. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
  5. Once boiling, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes, or until the beans are very tender and easily crushed between your fingers. Add more water during cooking if needed to keep the beans submerged.
  6. Once tender, remove the pot from heat. Stir in the granulated sugar and salt until fully dissolved. The soup should be sweet, but the salt helps to enhance the sweetness. Adjust sugar to your preference.
  7. While the zenzai is simmering, prepare the mochi. You can toast the mochi in a toaster oven, under a broiler, or in a dry pan until it puffs up and turns golden brown.
  8. Ladle the warm zenzai into individual serving bowls.
  9. Place 1-2 pieces of freshly toasted mochi into each bowl of zenzai.
  10. Serve immediately and enjoy the warmth and sweetness.
  11. For a thinner soup, add a little hot water; for a thicker soup, simmer uncovered for a few more minutes.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, you can add a small piece of kombu (dried kelp) during the simmering process and remove it before serving.
  • Adjust the sweetness to your liking; some prefer it very sweet, while others prefer a more subtle sweetness.
  • If you have access to a Dondoyaki bonfire, you can traditionally grill the mochi over the embers for an authentic smoky flavor.
